clue.text: Left badly placed with one in short race here

indicators.note: in says the single letter goes inside the letters around it

parts.note: ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated
put means placed
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A runner who started on the wrong side of the track takes part in a short race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short race here' looks like an athletics event; it is the land of tiny people in Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's island is inhabited by a diminutive people, a race of short folk.

clue.text: Ball starting 'slightly late causes flap

indicators.note: a word that starts late has lost its opening letter, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a globe is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: A ball that begins its flight a touch behind time causes a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flap' looks like the noun for a panic; here it is a hanging flap of flesh, such as the soft part of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An earlobe is a soft hanging flap of flesh, so lobe is a fair synonym.

clue.text: See message on earth from South American monument

parts.note: Lincoln is the seat of a bishop, a cathedral see
a memo is a short message

indicators.note: in a down clue, read from the south means read upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: a fox's earth is its lair

explanation.surface: An instruction to view a message about the planet sent from a South American monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one phrase but splits; 'from South' means read upwards in this down light, so the earth word reverses into a Middle Eastern currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Washington memorial to Abraham Lincoln is a famous monument in the United States.

clue.text: Tavern heard landlord dropping a name openly

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: an inn is a tavern

indicators.note: dropping says the following letters are removed from the landlord's word

parts.note: a publican is the landlord of a pub
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub landlord was overheard openly leaving out someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns INN into its sound-alike IN; 'dropping' takes A and N out of PUBLICAN to leave PUBLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in the open, before everyone, is doing it in public.

clue.text: Strip from rug in tatters

indicators.note: something in tatters is torn apart, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tears a strip from a rug that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in tatters' looks like the whole indicator, but 'in' is part of the fodder: RUG IN rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig a ship is to strip it of its rigging, so the verb means to strip.

clue.text: Prince eating fully prepared meat

indicators.note: eating says the prince's name takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V
all can mean fully, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A prince tucking into meat that has been properly prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is the madcap young Henry V of Shakespeare's history plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal meat is slaughtered and prepared according to Islamic law.

clue.text: Omitting page catches up with a rising novelist

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: omitting says the named letter is left out of the word that follows
in a down clue, rising says the pieces are read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: nets means catches

explanation.surface: A writer, leaving out a page, catches up after a rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Omitting page' takes P out of UP to leave U; NETS + U + A, turned by 'rising', reads NETSUA upwards, giving the writer of Emma.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen wrote Pride and Prejudice and Emma, so she is a novelist.

clue.text: Peer up and notice gunners within short distance leading sailor?

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
high means up
an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: within says the gunners go inside the shortened distance
short says the last letter is cut from the distance

parts.note: a mile is a distance
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: A nobleman looks up and sees artillerymen close by, behind a sailor out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the distance by its last letter and 'within' houses the gunners in it. The question mark flags that the title is a historic office, not a literal sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord High Admiral was the officer at the head of the English navy, a top seaman.

clue.text: Relieved when oil started flowing

indicators.note: flowing suggests liquid moving freely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People felt relief once the oil began to gush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relieved' is used as in fears laid to rest: put to an end, eased.
explanation.definitionFit: Fears that are laid to rest are dispelled, so the phrase means relieved or put at ease.

clue.text: Poet's upset wife from US State?

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, and a W turned over looks like M

parts.note: Delaware is a state of the USA

explanation.surface: A poet is distressed by a wife from an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the W of DELAWARE upside down so it becomes M. 'Poet's' reads as 'poet is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter de la Mare was an English poet, author of The Listeners.

clue.text: Bachelor getting on a bit finally became emperor

parts.note: taken as written
a part is a bit

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A single man, getting on a bit, at last rose to emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E, the last letter of 'became'.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: It may afford some returning from Gobi a rest

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Travellers coming back from the Gobi desert find somewhere to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the surface work together: a caravanserai affords a rest to travellers crossing the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai is a caravanserai, a lodging for travellers, which affords them rest.

clue.text: Slip ring into hairdo

indicators.note: into says the ring goes inside the hairdo

parts.note: a bob is a short hairstyle
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A ring gets caught in someone's hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' is a mistake, a boob in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is a blunder or error, so it is a synonym of slip in that sense.

clue.text: Hop's going crazy with' Great Balls of Fire

indicators.note: going crazy says the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hops going mad to the tune of the rock'n'roll song Great Balls of Fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Balls of Fire' looks like the song title, but 'Great' is fodder and 'Balls of Fire' is the definition: small shot fired from a cannon.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot is a cluster of small iron balls fired from a cannon.

clue.text: Pithy stuff from Dutch house hunter

parts.note: the House of Orange is the Dutch royal family
John Peel was a famous huntsman, of the song D'ye ken John Peel

explanation.surface: Something concise from a Dutch hunting family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pithy' looks like 'concise', but it means full of pith, the white layer under citrus skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin of a citrus fruit has white pith clinging to it, so it is literally pithy material.

clue.text: Working to suppress crack that keeps appearing

parts.note: running means working, as of a machine
to gag is to suppress

explanation.surface: A machine works to hold back a crack that keeps opening up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like a fissure; it is a wisecrack, a joke that recurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A running gag is a joke repeated throughout a show, a wisecrack that keeps coming back.

clue.text: Pinched check glove

parts.note: gaunt means pinched or haggard
a let is a hindrance or check, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A glove that has been stolen and checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' looks like 'stolen'; it means thin-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is a strong glove with a wide cuff, as worn with armour.

clue.text: Stravinsky's written one to do with horn, mostly

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to gore is to wound with a horn

explanation.surface: Stravinsky wrote a piece about a horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stravinsky's written' says how the composer's first name is spelt; 'horn' looks musical but is an animal's horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor was the first name of the composer of The Rite of Spring.

clue.text: Thing about me is I manage love badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters are put together wrongly and rearranged

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A confession that someone handles romance poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thing about me' is the definition: an obsession with oneself. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an obsessive preoccupation with oneself, a fixation with me.

clue.text: Called before wedding with soft vegetable

parts.note: née introduces a woman's maiden name, what she was called before marriage
p is piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A bride's former name served with a soft vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEP is Scots for a turnip or swede.
explanation.definitionFit: Neep is the Scottish word for a turnip, a root vegetable.

clue.text: "Lovely pot" noted shopper

parts.note: super means lovely or excellent
pot and grass are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a beautiful flowerpot while out shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shopper' looks like a customer; it is one who shops others to the police. A supergrass is a major informer.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them, and a supergrass is a top informer.

clue.text: Bully on wagon has not caught up

indicators.note: caught says the reversed word is held inside the other piece

parts.note: someone on the wagon is teetotal, TT

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read backwards

parts.note: nary means not one

explanation.surface: A bully riding on a wagon has not been caught yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the word for not backwards in this down light, and 'caught' sets it between the teetotaller's letters; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is an oppressive ruler, or anyone who bullies others.

clue.text: Intimate check on European Community and its environment

indicators.note: on says the first pieces sit after the abbreviation, placed on it

parts.note: cosy means intimate
to stem is to check a flow

explanation.surface: A close inspection of the European Community and its surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Community' reads as one phrase, but it splits: European gives the letter and 'Community and its environment' is the definition; 'on' sets the other pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecosystem is a biological community of organisms together with its physical surroundings.

clue.text: May entice crowds coming at first from all parts?

definitions.text: May entice crowds coming at first from all parts?

indicators.note: first takes the initial letter of each of the words that come before it

explanation.surface: A place that may draw people arriving from every corner.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'May entice crowds coming at' spell the answer, and the whole clue describes the holy city that draws pilgrims from everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Mecca draws pilgrims from all over the world, and the word is used for any place that attracts crowds.

clue.text: Might Met's leading pairs pretend to sing?

indicators.note: leading pairs takes the opening two letters of each word

explanation.surface: Might the Metropolitan Opera's principals only mouth the words?
explanation.walkthrough: MI from Might and ME from Met's. Met is the Metropolitan Opera, New York.
explanation.definitionFit: To mime is to act without words, such as mouthing to a recording rather than singing.

clue.text: A dip often seen in bridge

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between mountain peaks

explanation.surface: A dip often seen beneath a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' looks like a structure; it is the card game, where Acol is a common bidding system.
explanation.definitionFit: Acol is the standard bidding system played in British bridge.

clue.text: Andy was useful to her before Henry came along

definitions.text: Andy was useful to her before Henry came along

parts.words: Andy was useful to her before Henry came along
parts.note: the Cockney flower girl of Pygmalion dropped her aitches, so handy came out as Andy, until Professor Higgins taught her to speak

explanation.surface: Someone called Andy helped a woman until Henry turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shaw's Pygmalion (and My Fair Lady), Henry Higgins teaches the flower girl to pronounce her h's; Andy is her Cockney 'handy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's flower girl Eliza Doolittle says 'andy for handy before Higgins reforms her speech.

clue.text: Look at Latin books with endlessly ornate card

parts.note: ecce is Latin for look or behold
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: rich can mean ornate or elaborate

explanation.surface: Someone examines Latin books together with a fancy greetings card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' looks like a greetings card; it is an old word for an odd character.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an amusing or odd person, which is what an eccentric is.

clue.text: Sign needed by motorist following directions

definitions.text: Sign needed by motorist following directions

parts.words: Sign needed by motorist following directions
parts.note: a learner driver is still taking instructions from a teacher, and must display the red letter on a white board

explanation.surface: A road sign for a driver obeying instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver must display a square plate bearing a red L.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner driver, who follows an instructor's directions, displays this sign on the car.

clue.text: Soldier dropped lines to English girl, ultimately never meeting

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier dropped by parachute
L is a line, so LL is lines

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A paratrooper wrote to an English girl, but in the end they never met.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes L, the last letter of 'girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel lines never meet however far they are extended.
